meta.sample_size_note: n=7 candidates, 23 requirements, 161 (requirement x candidate) gold labels. Kendall tau and ranking-level numbers are illustrative only - NOT a statistically meaningful ranking benchmark.
labeling_rules: demonstrated: the requirement's skill appears with a concrete usage context (a project or experience bullet that names it in action).
claimed_only: the skill appears only on a skills-summary line, a coursework listing, or a bare tech-stack header without an application bullet; also used for 'Currently Learning' entries.
absent: no occurrence of the skill (or a defensible synonym) anywhere on the resume.

Language rules: concrete use of a language OR of a framework built on it counts as demonstrated for that language (e.g. Spring Boot -> Java, React.js -> JavaScript). A bare frameworks/skills line without a project counts as claimed_only.
DSA rule: a competitive/GATE problem-solving record (e.g. '800+ coding problems', 'GATE AIR 1374') counts as demonstrated; coursework-only counts as claimed_only.
cloud rule: only a named, used cloud service in a project (e.g. AWS S3, Supabase) counts as demonstrated; a 'cloud-based project' without a named platform counts as claimed_only.
borderline_examples: Spring Boot as Java evidence: Jainish/Gaurav/Kartavya/Mayank each shipped a Spring Boot backend project -> R04 Java = demonstrated. Keyur only lists Spring Boot under 'Currently Learning' -> R04 = claimed_only.

Concurrency vs literal multi-threading: Aditya ('concurrent client handling'), Mayank ('concurrency safety using fcntl file locking') and Keyur ('process synchronization and file locking') are counted demonstrated for R07 even though none says the word 'thread'; Jainish's Linux device-driver work (kernel, hardware-software integration, no explicit synchronization mention) is counted absent.

Cloud line: Jainish's 'AWS S3 for PDF storage' is demonstrated cloud usage; Mayank's Docker/K8s skills line is claimed_only (containerization claim, not a named cloud platform); Parva's 'Cloud Compiler on VMs' has no named cloud platform, so claimed_only despite the Cloud Computing coursework.
R14 Testing: only Keyur demonstrates it ('automated unit testing using Pytest integrated into Jenkins'); every other candidate has no testing-framework mention at all.
meta.methodology: Labels are hand-assigned by reading each candidate's full extracted text (pdfplumber) against the 23 gold requirements enumerated from the JD bullet list. Software/soft-skill bullets (communication, quick learner, understand requirements, 'software engineering best practices' as a whole) are excluded from the requirement space because they are not discretely verifiable on student resumes. The JD's Education requirement (M.S. pursuit) is excluded: all 7 candidates are IIIT Bangalore M.Tech/MTech students, so it carries no discriminating signal. Gold spans (gold_chunk_id + gold_quote) are recorded only for demonstrated labels; each gold_quote is a verbatim substring of the referenced chunk's raw_text (chunking by the real ResumeChunker v1).

system_skills_measured.note: Real extraction output (rule_based_fallback_extraction on JD/JD.pdf, LLM-less mode; OPENROUTER_API_KEY unset so gpt-4o-mini is skipped). The 11 extracted skills map onto 10 of the 23 gold requirement rows (R09 takes two); the other 13 rows have NO skill to key a verdict on, so the LLM-less system scores them 'absent' by default.
